properties.areaDesc: Maui County Leeward Waters
properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 28 at 2:40AM HST until October 28 at 3:45AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
SMWHFO

The National Weather Service in Honolulu has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Maui County Leeward Waters...

* Until 345 AM HST.

* At 237 AM HST, a strong thunderstorm was located 14 nm southeast of
FAD Buoy P, or 40 nm west of Lanai Airport, moving northeast at 15
knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves.

* The strong thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Prepare for gusty winds, steep and fast-building seas, and blinding
downpours. Stay low or go below, and make sure all on board are
wearing life jackets.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away

return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 27 at 2:20PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
Between 4 and 7 inches of heavy, wet, snow fell across the
Fairbanks Metro Area Monday. Warming temperatures Monday evening
into Tuesday have caused portions of that snowfall to melt,
creating many slushy areas of melting snow and pooling water.
Overnight low temperatures Tuesday night into Wednesday morning
are expected to fall into the upper teens to low 20s which will
allow much of this slush to refreeze. Slick surfaces are very
likely Wednesday morning as wet surfaces and small water puddles
freeze. Areas of heavy, wet snow will also refreeze giving the
slush a sturdier, more ice like texture. Travel may be impacted,
especially during the Wednesday morning commute.

Additional rain and snow showers are expected overnight Wednesday
into Thursday with much lighter accumulations than Monday. Less
than an inch of new snow is possible with only a few hundredths of
an inch of liquid equivalent expected.
